box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0px; text-align: left;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div:
How gestating ideas work:
First of all, there are two kinds of ideas. Concrete and abstract. Concrete idea could be a guitar riff or a drum passage, a vocal line. Abstract idea would be for
example, lyrics. In order for an abstract idea to be used on a track, it needs a concrete idea to make it happen. A special case of abstract idea is the coreTag dualism,
which makes the release TRUE. At least one idea on a black metal release must carry both a tag and its reverse value, forming the re-sacralising tag.
Each "Collective Action(BAND): Gestate" creates a set number of filler ideas, determined by the morale trait.
Then a band member actor interacts with the filler idea via Character Action (Band Member): Gestate action.
This upgrades it to a higher level (Sketchy, Good, Excellent), and infuses it with a tag owned by the actor instance.
The idea is now considered "complete", and it can be used on a track. Emergent tags are considered closed.
Another Gestate action with the same tag can be made to the same idea to give it the status of "honed", and upgrade its level by one or
open an emergent tag for it, in which case it is considered "progressive". The Band Member can be another one, in which case the idea is also duplicated..

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 555px; margin-left: 2px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0px; text-align: left;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div:
How gestating tracks work:
A single track is made of one or more completed ideas, and one of the ideas must have "concrete" status. An idea becomes concrete when it is tied to an aspect.
For example, lyrics need a voice to be concrete. A track can have at most three ideas behind a single aspect, but one or two are ideal. Third's a crowd (see the 2:3 rule).
The number of ideas is significant for a later stage, where due to hardware limitations of the band, ideas can get mushed together on the demo.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 625px; margin-left: 2px;

div.div:
Re-Sacralising Dualism Mechanic:
For a release to be considered "blackened", it must have a tag combination of tag-antitag somewhere in its layout.
The elites are looking for this pattern in the release, so "the score" is heavily influenced by it.
The dualism must substitute what is commonly regarded as positive with its polar opposite.

div.div:
Phases of recording where the sound gets potentially altered for outside reasons are marked with different color.
Demo tapes tend to gather a fuzzy background noise from bouncing and less than optimal recording environment.
This might create a sound that the audience likes, but won't carry into a professional recording.
During recording and post-production, the recording studio personnel and the record company executives can also
damage the original sound.
